blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre historiografia a partir de um resumo acadêmico, reconhecendo a estrutura argumentativa e a linguagem de cautela.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Abstract: Whose Archive? Reading Silences in Colonial Records
paras: This article **interrogates** the assumption that colonial archives **neutrally record** events. Drawing on customs ledgers and petitions from three port cities, it **argues** that the silences in these records are **themselves evidence**: who was **left unnamed**, which complaints were **filed away**, and how clerks **normalized** violence in bureaucratic prose.

The analysis **suggests**, **though it cannot prove**, that petitioners **adapted** their language to what officials would hear. It **contributes to** a growing body of work on **archival agency**, and it **cautions** historians against **reading documents at face value**. **Further research is needed** on private papers, which may **complicate** the picture.

items.q: The article treats archives as neutral records.
Silences in records can themselves be evidence.
The authors claim to prove that petitioners adapted their language.

blocks.cap: Estrutura e cautela num resumo acadêmico

blocks.body: Resumos acadêmicos seguem o percurso **problema → método → tese → cautela → contribuição**. Verbos como *suggest, indicate, point to* **graduam o compromisso**.
*Argues* (defende com argumentos) ≠ *proves*. Não use *prove* para ciências humanas, salvo evidência decisiva.

items.s: The article ___ the assumption that archives are neutral. (interrogate)
___ on customs ledgers, it argues that silences are evidence. (draw)
The analysis suggests, ___ it cannot prove, a shift. (though)
Further research is ___ on private papers. (need)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: It reads the silences as evidence

body: **Read between the lines.** — Ler nas entrelinhas.
**Take at face value.** — Aceitar ao pé da letra.
**Paint a fuller picture.** — Compor um quadro mais completo.
**Shed light on.** — Lançar luz sobre.
**Against the grain.** — A contrapelo.
**Set the record straight.** — Corrigir os fatos.
**Leave a paper trail.** — Deixar rastro documental.
**In hindsight.** — Em retrospecto.
**Gloss over.** — Passar por cima.
**Rewrite history.** — Reescrever a história.
**Does the article prove that petitioners adapted?** — O artigo prova que os peticionários se adaptaram?
**What is its main contribution?** — Qual é sua principal contribuição?
**It reads the silences as evidence.** — Lê os silêncios como evidência.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence abstract for an imaginary article in the humanities, including a thesis, a source, a caution and a limit.
blocks.model: This article examines how nineteenth-century railway timetables shaped local identity. Drawing on station archives and passenger letters, it argues that punctuality became a civic virtue. The evidence suggests, though it does not prove, that rural towns resisted standard time longer than cities. The study contributes to work on infrastructure and everyday life. It cautions against assuming uniform adoption. Further research is needed on women’s travel diaries.
